business_problem: BBVA needed a scalable, governed way to accelerate the development, validation and deployment of AI models across the Group while preserving traceability, security, risk controls and existing approval processes in a regulated financial environment.
solution_summary: BBVA implemented a new MLOps architecture with AWS inside ADA, its global cloud-based data and artificial intelligence platform, to standardize and speed the machine learning lifecycle across the bank. ADA serves as the shared platform layer for more than 6,500 users, including 1,000 data scientists, while Amazon SageMaker AI provides the cloud machine learning environment used to build, train, deploy and manage models. The architecture creates ephemeral development environments so multiple teams can experiment and validate functionality in parallel without affecting shared setups, then automatically removes resources after testing. It also automates operational tasks plus validation, traceability and control processes, and maintains a centralized audit trail for security and transparency. Approved models are integrated into BBVA’s technology operations for use cases such as personalized recommendations and financial forecasting.

data_flow: Within ADA, BBVA teams create and test machine learning solutions in ephemeral Amazon SageMaker AI environments, run automated validation, traceability and control checks, record lifecycle evidence in a centralized audit trail, and then move approved models into BBVA’s production technology operations for use cases such as personalized recommendations and financial forecasting.
business_outcome: BBVA accelerated AI model delivery across the Group, enabled greater team autonomy and component reuse, reduced infrastructure operating costs, and strengthened governed, auditable deployment of AI solutions in production.
